cc-prog1-aligned.label: ALIGNED
cc-prog1-aligned.explanation: The CLO states observable Java programming performance (develop and test) suited to a Year 2 fundamentals course.

cc-prog1-keyword.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
cc-prog1-keyword.sourceQuote: vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society
cc-prog1-keyword.targetQuote: Appreciate the history of programming and understand the importance of programming in society.
cc-prog1-keyword.explanation: The CLO uses non-observable verbs ("Appreciate", "understand") that cannot be assessed directly. It stays at Remember/Understand level, below what a Year 2 programming course needs. It names programming and society but states no performance of programming or logical formulation. It covers only the description's societal-role aspect and leaves out Java fundamentals, logic and coding practices.
cc-prog1-keyword.draft: Explain the role of computers and programmers in society by describing real-world applications of Java programs, and apply good coding practices when writing them.

cc-prog1-offsubject.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cc-prog1-offsubject.sourceQuote: Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming
cc-prog1-offsubject.targetQuote: Design and analyze a relational database schema using normalization up to third normal form.
cc-prog1-offsubject.explanation: The CLO is about relational database design and normalization, which is a database subject. The course description covers Java programming fundamentals, logical formulation and coding practices, and does not mention databases or schema design. Its Analyze/Create level also exceeds a fundamentals course. The CLO needs content the description does not cover.
cc-prog1-offsubject.draft: Design algorithms using flowcharts or pseudocode and implement them as Java programs that use methods and arrays to solve simple problems.

cc-prog1-generic.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cc-prog1-generic.sourceQuote: foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming
cc-prog1-generic.targetQuote: Demonstrate professionalism and teamwork in the workplace.
cc-prog1-generic.explanation: The CLO is a generic workplace outcome that would fit any course. It names no programming, Java or logical formulation competence from the description. "Demonstrate professionalism" is not tied to any observable programming task, and teamwork is not part of the description.
cc-prog1-generic.draft: Apply logical formulation techniques and good coding practices, such as meaningful naming and documentation, when writing Java programs.

cc-prog1-real1.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
cc-prog1-real1.targetQuote: Define and analyze the computing requirements needed for an effective solution
cc-prog1-real1.explanation: The target CLO is generic and would fit any computing course: it names no programming, Java or coding competence, so the course subject is missing (test 1). "Define and analyze" is observable, but it asks for requirements analysis, which the source description does not cover; the description stresses logical formulation, Java fundamentals and good coding practices (test 3). It also never states a performance such as writing or testing code. "Holistic and impactful solutions" is vague and not assessable.
cc-prog1-real1.draft: Analyze a problem and design a logical solution, then implement it as a Java program that applies good coding practices.

cc-prog1-unreadable.label: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
cc-prog1-unreadable.targetQuote: Xq zv wl kjh pqrt mnb vcx.
cc-prog1-unreadable.explanation: The target CLO text is unreadable: it is a string of meaningless characters and states no competence, so it cannot be judged against the course.

cs-prog1-aligned.label: ALIGNED
cs-prog1-aligned.explanation: The CLOs cover Java fundamentals, problem decomposition, debugging and good practice without overlap, and none is too broad.

cs-prog1-redundant.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
cs-prog1-redundant.sourceQuote: logical formulation techniques essential for programming
cs-prog1-redundant.targetQuote: CLO 2: Develop Java programs that use loop statements.
cs-prog1-redundant.explanation: CLOs 1, 2, 3 and 4 all ask for the same competence, writing Java programs with loops, in different words. The set also leaves out the rest of the Java fundamentals the description promises (variables, conditionals, methods), logical formulation techniques, good coding practices and real-world applications.
cs-prog1-redundant.draft: Merge CLOs 1-4 into one loop CLO and add CLOs on logical problem formulation, other Java fundamentals, and good coding practices.

cp-bsit-aligned.label: ALIGNED
cp-bsit-aligned.explanation: The CLO has the student write, compile and debug Java programs in an IDE, which is using a modern computing tool at Apply level.

cp-bsit-keyword.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cp-bsit-keyword.sourceQuote: Analyze complex problems, and identify and define the computing requirements
cp-bsit-keyword.targetQuote: Memorize the keywords and syntax of the Java language.
cp-bsit-keyword.explanation: The PO asks the student to analyze problems and define computing requirements for a solution (Analyze). The CLO only asks to memorize Java keywords and syntax (Remember). Its action verb and Bloom level are lower than the PO's. It shows no problem analysis or requirements definition. It shares only the computing topic. The CLO text must change.
cp-bsit-keyword.draft: Analyze a programming problem and define its requirements, then apply Java keywords and syntax to design a program that solves it.

cp-bsit-wrongpo.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cp-bsit-wrongpo.targetQuote: Develop and test Java programs that use loops and conditional statements.
cp-bsit-wrongpo.explanation: The PO is about preserving and promoting Filipino historical and cultural heritage. The CLO develops and tests Java programs with loops and conditionals, which is a sound programming outcome with a different subject. The tag does not fit, so the PO choice is wrong, not the CLO.

cp-bsit-real3.label: ALIGNED
cp-bsit-real3.targetQuote: Collaborate effectively within multi-disciplinary and culturally diverse teams
cp-bsit-real3.explanation: The CLO states that students collaborate effectively in multi-disciplinary, culturally diverse teams, which matches the PO's teamwork competence.

cc-syseng-aligned.label: ALIGNED
cc-syseng-aligned.targetQuote: Develop a system requirements specification and a functional decomposition
cc-syseng-aligned.explanation: The target CLO states an observable Create-level performance (develop a requirements specification and functional decomposition) that matches the source's requirements analysis and systems design topics at year 4.

cc-syseng-keyword.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
cc-syseng-keyword.sourceQuote: focusing on the analysis, design, and management of complex systems
cc-syseng-keyword.explanation: The target CLO only repeats the course title. 'Describe' is a Remember/Understand verb too low for a year 4 course that focuses on analysis, design and management of complex systems. It names no object (concepts, process, system type) and gives no performance that can be assessed against the source's topics such as requirements, integration or performance evaluation.
cc-syseng-keyword.draft: Apply systems engineering principles to analyze requirements, design and integrate the components of a complex system, and evaluate its performance against stakeholder needs and operational constraints.

cc-syseng-offsubject.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cc-syseng-offsubject.sourceQuote: principles and practices of systems engineering
cc-syseng-offsubject.targetQuote: Write Java programs that use loops and conditional statements.
cc-syseng-offsubject.explanation: The target CLO is about computer programming in Java (loops and conditionals), a different subject from the source's systems engineering. It matches none of the source's topics (requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, performance evaluation). Its Apply verb fits, but the subject does not belong to this course.
cc-syseng-offsubject.draft: Design an integrated system architecture for a complex engineering problem that satisfies stakeholder requirements and operational constraints.

cc-syseng-real2.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
cc-syseng-real2.sourceQuote: large-scale engineering problems involving multiple components, stakeholders, and operational constraints
cc-syseng-real2.targetQuote: Apply critical and creative thinking skills to analyze, design, and optimize complex systems
cc-syseng-real2.explanation: The target CLO is in the right subject, with Analyze/Create-level verbs and a system with components, but it is generic: 'critical and creative thinking skills' would fit any course. It names no systems engineering content from the source (requirements, stakeholders, integration, project management, performance evaluation). It bundles three verbs (analyze, design, optimize) in one outcome, which makes it hard to assess as a single performance.
cc-syseng-real2.draft: Analyze stakeholder requirements and design and integrate the people, materials, technology and information components of a complex system, and optimize its performance within operational constraints.

cs-syseng-narrow.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
cs-syseng-narrow.sourceQuote: Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and performance evaluation.
cs-syseng-narrow.targetQuote: CLO 4: Maintain a requirements traceability matrix.
cs-syseng-narrow.explanation: The CLOs cover only requirements work. CLO 1-4 all sit in requirements analysis (eliciting, writing, tracing, and maintaining requirements), so CLO 3 and CLO 4 largely repeat the same traceability competence. The description also promises systems design, integration, project management and performance evaluation, and no CLO covers any of these. The set does not cover the essential learning the title and description promise.
cs-syseng-narrow.draft: Merge CLO 3 and CLO 4 into one traceability CLO, and add CLOs for systems design and integration, project management, and performance evaluation of complex systems.

cp-bsie-wrongpo.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cp-bsie-wrongpo.targetQuote: Develop a system requirements specification and a functional decomposition
cp-bsie-wrongpo.explanation: The PO asks for the ability to function on multidisciplinary teams. The CLO is a sound outcome about producing a requirements specification and a functional decomposition, but it states no teamwork, collaboration or multidisciplinary activity. The PO named here is not the one this CLO develops, so the tag does not fit and should be changed.

cp-bsie-real2.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
cp-bsie-real2.sourceQuote: Ability to design a system, component, or process to meet desired needs within realistic constraints
cp-bsie-real2.targetQuote: analyze, design, and optimize complex systems
cp-bsie-real2.explanation: The CLO shares the design verb and the subject of complex systems. It is missing the design-to-meet-needs element and any realistic constraints (economic, environmental, social, ethical, health and safety, sustainability), and it does not mention standards. Its Bloom level, with optimize and design, is adequate, but the PO's constraints and standards are not shown.
cp-bsie-real2.draft: Apply critical and creative thinking skills to analyze, design, and optimize complex systems that meet stakeholder needs within realistic constraints and applicable standards, integrating various components such as people, materials, technology, and information.

cc-sensors-aligned.label: ALIGNED
cc-sensors-aligned.targetQuote: Select and condition a sensor signal
cc-sensors-aligned.explanation: The CLO states an observable, Apply-level performance on sensor conditioning and ADC interfacing, which matches the course description and a year 3 level.

cc-sensors-keyword.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
cc-sensors-keyword.sourceQuote: construction and operation of sensors and transducers
cc-sensors-keyword.targetQuote: Explain the importance of sensors in modern society.
cc-sensors-keyword.explanation: The CLO is about the course subject (sensors), but "Explain the importance of sensors in modern society" is a generic Understand-level statement. It describes no technical performance with sensors, transducers, signal conversion or the other devices in the description. It is below the Apply focus of the description for a year 3 course, and it is weakly assessable because it needs no engineering competence.
cc-sensors-keyword.draft: Explain the construction and operation of sensors and transducers and select suitable sensors for converting physical parameters into electrical signals in measurement and control applications.

cc-sensors-offsubject.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cc-sensors-offsubject.sourceQuote: application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits
cc-sensors-offsubject.targetQuote: Apply queueing theory to model production lines.
cc-sensors-offsubject.explanation: Queueing theory for production line modeling belongs to operations research or industrial engineering. The course description covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices, sensors, transducers and actuators, none of which relates to queueing models.
cc-sensors-offsubject.draft: Apply operational amplifiers and signal converters to develop signal conversion circuits that allow measurement and control of physical parameters by a digital processing system.

cc-sensors-real3.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
cc-sensors-real3.sourceQuote: application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits
cc-sensors-real3.targetQuote: design, test, and optimize mixed-signal and sensor applications
cc-sensors-real3.explanation: The CLO is in the right area (mixed-signal and sensor applications), but it has gaps against the course description. (1) Its first half, 'behavior of passive components in AC circuits', is circuit-analysis content that the description does not cover. The description names op-amps, signal converters, power switching devices, sensors, transducers and actuators. (2) It names no course devices such as op-amps, ADC/DAC converters, sensors or transducers, nor the measurement, processing and control of physical parameters by digital systems. (3) It packs several verbs (analyze, apply, design, test, optimize) and a teamwork condition into one outcome, so it is hard to assess. 'Optimize' goes beyond what the description promises at year 3. (4) 'engineering solutions' is generic and would fit any engineering course.
cc-sensors-real3.draft: Design and test signal conversion circuits using operational amplifiers, signal converters and sensors or transducers in multidisciplinary teams, to measure, process and control physical parameters with digital processing systems.

cs-sensors-redundant.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
cs-sensors-redundant.sourceQuote: construction and operation of sensors and transducers
cs-sensors-redundant.targetQuote: CLO 2: Describe how a sensor changes a physical parameter into an electrical signal.
cs-sensors-redundant.explanation: CLO 1, CLO 2, CLO 3 and CLO 4 all ask for the same competence (explaining how sensors or transducers convert physical parameters into electrical signals) in different words, which breaks the no-repetition test. The set also leaves out major blocks the description promises: operational amplifiers, signal converters (ADC/DAC), power switching devices, designing signal conversion circuits for digital processing systems, and actuators. The conversion from electrical signal back to a physical parameter (vice-versa) is not covered either. All the verbs are low level (Explain, Describe, Discuss, Outline), though the description stresses application for a year 3 course.
cs-sensors-redundant.draft: Merge CLO 1-4 into one outcome on sensor and transducer operation, and add CLOs on operational amplifier circuits, signal converters, power switching devices, signal conversion circuit design for digital systems, and actuators.

cs-sensors-generic.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cs-sensors-generic.sourceQuote: construction and operation of sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals
cs-sensors-generic.explanation: CLO 1 (professionalism), CLO 2 (teamwork), CLO 3 (communication) and CLO 4 (lifelong learning) are generic outcomes that would fit any course. None mentions operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices, sensors, transducers, actuators or signal conversion circuits, so the essential learning in the title and description is not covered. The CLOs also share the same verb 'Demonstrate' with no technical object, so they are vague and not assessable.
cs-sensors-generic.draft: Replace these with subject-specific CLOs on operational amplifier circuits, signal converters, power switching devices, sensors and transducers, signal conversion circuits for digital systems, and actuators.

cp-bscpe-aligned.label: ALIGNED
cp-bscpe-aligned.targetQuote: Design and conduct experiments to characterize sensor accuracy and analyze and interpret the measurement data
cp-bscpe-aligned.explanation: The CLO states designing and conducting experiments and analyzing and interpreting data, on sensor accuracy, matching the PO.

cp-bscpe-keyword.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cp-bscpe-keyword.sourceQuote: Ability to design and conduct experiments, as well as to analyze and interpret data
cp-bscpe-keyword.targetQuote: Discuss experiments in the history of sensor technology.
cp-bscpe-keyword.explanation: The CLO only shares the word 'experiments' with the PO. Its verb 'Discuss' is Understand level, below the PO's design, conduct, analyze and interpret. It asks for no design or conduct of experiments and no data analysis or interpretation. Its subject, the history of sensor technology, is not performing experiments or handling data.
cp-bscpe-keyword.draft: Design and conduct experiments on sensor performance, and analyze and interpret the resulting measurement data.

cp-bscpe-wrongpo.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cp-bscpe-wrongpo.targetQuote: Calibrate a sensor and record its measurement tolerance.
cp-bscpe-wrongpo.explanation: The source PO asks for effective communication. The target CLO develops a technical measurement competence (calibrating a sensor, recording tolerance). It does not state any communicating, such as reporting to an audience, writing or presenting. Recording a tolerance is data logging, not communication, so the link would rest on an activity the CLO does not mention. The CLO is a sound outcome for this sensors course, so the PO tag does not fit and should be changed.

cc-prog1-aligned.label: ALIGNED
cc-prog1-aligned.explanation: The CLO states an observable Apply-level performance in Java fundamentals, which fits the course description and a year 2 introductory course.

cc-prog1-keyword.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
cc-prog1-keyword.sourceQuote: vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society
cc-prog1-keyword.targetQuote: Appreciate the history of programming and understand the importance of programming in society.
cc-prog1-keyword.explanation: The CLO uses "Appreciate" and "understand", which are not observable, assessable verbs and sit at Remember/Understand level. It does not state a performance in programming. It touches only the description's role of computers in society and leaves out the core of the course: Java fundamentals, logical formulation and good coding practices. History of programming is not covered by the description.
cc-prog1-keyword.draft: Explain the role of computers and programmers in society by describing real-world applications of Java programs and the good coding practices used to build them.

cc-prog1-offsubject.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cc-prog1-offsubject.sourceQuote: Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming
cc-prog1-offsubject.targetQuote: Design and analyze a relational database schema using normalization up to third normal form.
cc-prog1-offsubject.explanation: The CLO is about relational database design and normalization, which is a different subject from Java programming fundamentals. The course description does not cover database content. The Analyze/Create level also exceeds what an introductory programming course asks for. The draft moves the CLO toward the course's own subject.
cc-prog1-offsubject.draft: Design and implement Java programs that apply logical formulation techniques, such as algorithms and flowcharts, to solve simple real-world problems.

cc-prog1-generic.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cc-prog1-generic.sourceQuote: foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming
cc-prog1-generic.targetQuote: Demonstrate professionalism and teamwork in the workplace.
cc-prog1-generic.explanation: The CLO is a generic workplace outcome that would fit any course. It names no programming competence, no Java and no logical formulation. The description does not cover workplace professionalism or teamwork. The verb "Demonstrate" has no stated object that can be assessed in this subject.
cc-prog1-generic.draft: Apply good coding practices, such as meaningful naming, comments and consistent structure, when writing Java programs that solve simple problems.

cc-prog1-real1.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
cc-prog1-real1.sourceQuote: foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming
cc-prog1-real1.targetQuote: Define and analyze the computing requirements needed for an effective solution
cc-prog1-real1.explanation: The target CLO is generic: it names no programming, Java or coding performance, so it would fit any computing course. 'Define and analyze the computing requirements' is a requirements-engineering/systems-analysis competence, not the programming fundamentals and logical formulation that the source description promises. The phrase 'holistic and impactful solutions' is vague and not assessable. Analysis of requirements for a solution is beyond what a Year 2 introductory Java course teaches, and the description does not cover it. The draft keeps the author's idea of analyzing requirements but ties it to a Java program.
cc-prog1-real1.draft: Analyze a simple problem to identify its inputs, processes and outputs, and design and implement a Java program that solves it effectively.

cc-prog1-unreadable.label: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
cc-prog1-unreadable.sourceQuote: Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming
cc-prog1-unreadable.targetQuote: Xq zv wl kjh pqrt mnb vcx.
cc-prog1-unreadable.explanation: The target CLO text is unreadable gibberish and states no outcome, so it cannot be judged against the course.

cs-prog1-aligned.label: ALIGNED
cs-prog1-aligned.targetQuote: Decompose a problem into methods and implement them.
cs-prog1-aligned.explanation: The CLOs cover Java basics, decomposition, debugging and documentation without repeating each other.

cs-prog1-redundant.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cs-prog1-redundant.targetQuote: CLO 1: Write Java programs using loops.
cs-prog1-redundant.explanation: CLOs 1, 2, 3 and 4 all ask for the same competence, writing Java programs with loops, in different words. The set omits the rest of the essential learning in the description: variables, data types, conditionals, methods, logical formulation, good coding practices and real-world applications. The CLOs are also all at a similar Apply level, with no debugging, documentation or problem-solving outcome.
cs-prog1-redundant.draft: Merge CLOs 1-4 into one loop CLO and add distinct CLOs for logical problem formulation, conditionals and methods, good coding practices and debugging, and real-world applications.

cp-bsit-aligned.label: ALIGNED
cp-bsit-aligned.explanation: The CLO has students write, compile and debug Java programs in an IDE, which is using a modern computing tool, at Apply level.

cp-bsit-keyword.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cp-bsit-keyword.sourceQuote: Analyze complex problems, and identify and define the computing requirements
cp-bsit-keyword.targetQuote: Memorize the keywords and syntax of the Java language.
cp-bsit-keyword.explanation: The PO asks students to analyze complex problems and identify and define computing requirements for a solution (Analyze). The CLO only asks them to memorize Java keywords and syntax (Remember). So: (1) it has no analyze, identify or define action; (2) its Bloom level is far below the PO's; (3) its object is language syntax, not problems or requirements. It shares only a topic area with the PO.
cp-bsit-keyword.draft: Analyze a given problem, identify and define its computing requirements, and apply Java syntax and keywords to design a program that solves it.

cp-bsit-wrongpo.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cp-bsit-wrongpo.sourceQuote: Preserve and promote “Filipino historical and cultural heritage
cp-bsit-wrongpo.targetQuote: Develop and test Java programs that use loops and conditional statements.
cp-bsit-wrongpo.explanation: The PO is about preserving and promoting Filipino historical and cultural heritage. The CLO is a sound programming outcome: developing and testing Java programs with loops and conditionals. It develops no heritage or cultural competence, so the PO named here is not the one it develops and the tag does not fit.

cp-bsit-real3.label: ALIGNED
cp-bsit-real3.explanation: The CLO has students collaborate in multi-disciplinary, culturally diverse teams, matching the PO's teamwork and multi-cultural focus.

cc-syseng-aligned.label: ALIGNED
cc-syseng-aligned.explanation: The CLO develops a requirements specification and functional decomposition, which are core systems engineering competences named in the course description (requirements analysis, systems design), at a suitable Create level for year 4.

cc-syseng-keyword.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
cc-syseng-keyword.sourceQuote: analysis, design, and management of complex systems
cc-syseng-keyword.explanation: The CLO repeats the course title without stating a performance. "Describe" is a Remember/Understand level, too low for a year 4 course focused on analysis, design and management of complex systems. It names no object (requirements, design, integration, evaluation) and no assessable product, and it is so generic it would fit any introduction to the subject.
cc-syseng-keyword.draft: Analyze a complex engineered system by identifying its components, stakeholders and operational constraints, and evaluate its performance against defined requirements.

cc-syseng-offsubject.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cc-syseng-offsubject.sourceQuote: principles and practices of systems engineering
cc-syseng-offsubject.targetQuote: Write Java programs that use loops and conditional statements.
cc-syseng-offsubject.explanation: The CLO is about computer programming in Java (loops and conditionals), which is a different subject. The description covers requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management and performance evaluation, and none of these involve Java programming. The course description does not cover this content.
cc-syseng-offsubject.draft: Design the integration of the components of a complex engineered system by applying systems engineering methods to meet stakeholder requirements and operational constraints.

cc-syseng-real2.label: ALIGNED
cc-syseng-real2.sourceQuote: analysis, design, and management of complex systems
cc-syseng-real2.targetQuote: analyze, design, and optimize complex systems
cc-syseng-real2.explanation: The CLO applies analysis, design and optimization to complex systems and integrates their components, matching the course focus at a suitable Apply/Create level for year 4.

cs-syseng-narrow.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
cs-syseng-narrow.sourceQuote: Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and performance evaluation.
cs-syseng-narrow.targetQuote: CLO 4: Maintain a requirements traceability matrix.
cs-syseng-narrow.explanation: The CLOs together cover only requirements work (CLO 1-4). The description also promises systems design, integration, project management and performance evaluation, and none of these has a CLO. CLO 2, CLO 3 and CLO 4 are narrow, overlapping requirements-management steps (writing, tracing and maintaining a traceability matrix). CLO 3 and CLO 4 both ask for traceability. CLO 2 to CLO 4 are very low-level and sit below the analysis, design and management level expected in year 4.
cs-syseng-narrow.draft: Merge CLO 3 and CLO 4 into one traceability CLO, and add CLOs for designing and integrating a system architecture, managing a systems project, and evaluating system performance.

cp-bsie-wrongpo.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cp-bsie-wrongpo.sourceQuote: Ability to function on multidisciplinary teams
cp-bsie-wrongpo.targetQuote: Develop a system requirements specification and a functional decomposition
cp-bsie-wrongpo.explanation: The PO asks for functioning on multidisciplinary teams, which is a teamwork competence. The CLO develops a technical competence: writing a system requirements specification and a functional decomposition. It mentions no teamwork, collaboration or multidisciplinary roles. The CLO is a sound outcome for the course, but this PO is not the one it develops (a design PO would fit better). The tag does not fit, so retag the outcome and leave the CLO text unchanged.

cp-bsie-real2.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
cp-bsie-real2.sourceQuote: Ability to design a system, component, or process to meet desired needs within realistic constraints
cp-bsie-real2.targetQuote: analyze, design, and optimize complex systems
cp-bsie-real2.explanation: The CLO has the design verb and reaches Bloom Create, so it meets the PO's level, and the subject (complex systems) fits. Gaps: the CLO names no realistic constraints (economic, ethical, health and safety, sustainability) and no standards, so it does not show designing to meet desired needs within constraints. It also says nothing about meeting needs, which is the PO's purpose.
cp-bsie-real2.draft: Apply critical and creative thinking skills to analyze, design, and optimize complex systems that meet stakeholder needs within realistic constraints and applicable standards, integrating various components such as people, materials, technology, and information.

cc-sensors-aligned.label: ALIGNED
cc-sensors-aligned.targetQuote: Select and condition a sensor signal
cc-sensors-aligned.explanation: The CLO states an observable performance (select, condition, interface via ADC) that belongs to this course's sensor and signal conversion subject at a suitable year-3 Apply level.

cc-sensors-keyword.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
cc-sensors-keyword.sourceQuote: The course focuses on the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits
cc-sensors-keyword.targetQuote: Explain the importance of sensors in modern society.
cc-sensors-keyword.explanation: The CLO names sensors, which is the course subject, but it asks only to explain their importance in society, a general Understand-level statement. It does not state what the student does with sensors, transducers or signal conversion circuits. It is too low for year 3 and the description's application focus, and it would fit any course that mentions sensors.
cc-sensors-keyword.draft: Explain the operation of sensors and transducers and apply them in signal conversion circuits that convert physical parameters into electrical signals for measurement by a digital system.

cc-sensors-offsubject.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cc-sensors-offsubject.sourceQuote: operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices
cc-sensors-offsubject.targetQuote: Apply queueing theory to model production lines.
cc-sensors-offsubject.explanation: The CLO is about queueing theory and production line modelling, which is operations research or industrial engineering. The description covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices, sensors and actuators. No topic in the description needs queueing theory.
cc-sensors-offsubject.draft: Apply operational amplifiers and signal converters to build circuits that condition sensor signals for measurement and control by a digital system.

cc-sensors-real3.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
cc-sensors-real3.targetQuote: design, test, and optimize mixed-signal and sensor applications
cc-sensors-real3.explanation: The target CLO is partly in the course's subject: it names mixed-signal and sensor applications and uses observable verbs (design, test, optimize). However, (1) its first half, analyzing and applying passive components in AC circuits, is a circuit-theory topic that the source description does not list; the description covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices, sensors/transducers and actuators. (2) It never names the course's core devices (op-amps, converters, sensors, transducers) or the measurement, processing and control of physical parameters by digital systems. (3) 'In multidisciplinary teams' and 'for engineering solutions' are generic, add no assessable competence and would fit any course. (4) 'Analyze and apply' plus 'design, test, and optimize' bundle too many verbs, and 'optimize' is not clearly supported by the description.
cc-sensors-real3.draft: Design and test signal conversion circuits using operational amplifiers, signal converters and sensors or transducers to measure, process and control physical parameters through a digital processing system.

cs-sensors-redundant.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
cs-sensors-redundant.sourceQuote: operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices
cs-sensors-redundant.targetQuote: CLO 2: Describe how a sensor changes a physical parameter into an electrical signal.
cs-sensors-redundant.explanation: CLO 1, CLO 2, CLO 3 and CLO 4 all ask for the same competence (explaining how sensors or transducers convert physical parameters into electrical signals) in different words. The set also leaves out operational amplifiers, signal converters (ADC/DAC), power switching devices, signal conversion circuits for digital processing, and actuators. All four CLOs sit at Understand level, with no Apply or higher CLO for building or using circuits, which is weak for year 3.
cs-sensors-redundant.draft: Merge CLOs 1-4 into one CLO on sensor and transducer operation, and add CLOs on applying op-amps and signal converters, designing signal conversion circuits for digital systems, and actuators and power switching.

cs-sensors-generic.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cs-sensors-generic.sourceQuote: construction and operation of sensors and transducers
cs-sensors-generic.explanation: CLO 1, CLO 2, CLO 3 and CLO 4 (professionalism, teamwork, communication, lifelong learning) are generic outcomes that would fit any course. None addresses operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices, sensors and transducers, signal conversion circuits or actuators. The essential learning the title and description promise is not covered.
cs-sensors-generic.draft: Add subject-specific CLOs, for example on applying op-amps and signal converters, building sensor signal conditioning circuits, and interfacing sensors and actuators with digital systems.

cp-bscpe-aligned.label: ALIGNED
cp-bscpe-aligned.targetQuote: Design and conduct experiments to characterize sensor accuracy
cp-bscpe-aligned.explanation: The CLO statement has the PO's design, conduct, analyze and interpret verbs, applied to sensor measurement data.

cp-bscpe-keyword.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cp-bscpe-keyword.sourceQuote: design and conduct experiments, as well as to analyze and interpret data
cp-bscpe-keyword.targetQuote: Discuss experiments in the history of sensor technology.
cp-bscpe-keyword.explanation: The CLO statement only shares the word "experiments" with the PO. "Discuss" is Understand level, below the PO's design and conduct (Create) and analyze and interpret (Analyze). The CLO does not state designing, conducting, analyzing or interpreting, and its subject is the history of sensor technology rather than performing experiments and handling data.
cp-bscpe-keyword.draft: Design and conduct experiments on sensors and analyze and interpret the resulting measurement data.

cp-bscpe-wrongpo.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cp-bscpe-wrongpo.targetQuote: Calibrate a sensor and record its measurement tolerance.
cp-bscpe-wrongpo.explanation: The source PO asks for effective communication. The target CLO is about calibrating a sensor and recording its tolerance, which is a technical measurement competence in this course. Test 1 fails: the CLO has no communicating verb such as presenting, explaining or documenting for an audience. Test 3 fails: its subject is sensor calibration, not communication. 'Record' only means noting values, not communicating them. The CLO is sound for this course, so the PO tag does not fit and should be changed rather than the CLO text.
